briefdescription.para: Whether the console output uses colours.

detaileddescription.para: Set by --colour[=<when>], or by its American spelling --color[=<when>], as in the GNU tools, where <when> is always, never, or auto, or one of their GNU synonyms (yes and force, no and none, tty and if-tty), and --colour alone means always; the value is accepted only after =, and a mode word in the next argument, such as --colour never, is reported as an error, since it was probably meant as the value (an application argument of that kind can follow --). The alternative --use-colour=<mode> or --use-colour <mode>, also spelled --use-color, as in Catch2 and Boost UT, takes yes, no, or auto, and also accepts the other values of --colour. Used only by the human-readable reporter.

briefdescription.para: The patterns that select the suites and the test cases to run, one per nesting level.

detaileddescription.para: Each --filter=<pattern> or --filter <pattern> option adds one pattern; unlike the other options, --filter may be repeated. As with --grep in node-tap, the first pattern applies to the suite names, the second to the names of the test cases, and each further pattern to the names of the test cases nested one level deeper; the levels without a pattern are not filtered.

Within a pattern, | separates alternatives; a name matches when it matches any of them, as defined by utility::is_match(): * matches any sequence of characters, ? matches any single character, the match is case-sensitive, and the alternative must cover the whole name.

The suites and the test cases that do not match are reported as skipped, and their bodies are not called. The top suite is never skipped as a whole, since its body is main(), but when its name does not match the first pattern, all its test cases are skipped.
When the list is empty (the default), everything runs.

briefdescription.para: Whether to display the usage and the list of the options, instead of running the tests.

detaileddescription.para: Set by the --help option, or by its short form -h, which is the only short option. The runner then writes, on the console, the usage and the list of the options, runs no test, creates no output file, and run_suites() returns 0, or 2 after an option error. The text is written also with the silent verbosity, since it was requested.

briefdescription.para: Whether the test cases are listed instead of run.

detaileddescription.para: Set by the --list-tests option, or by its short form --list. When set, the suite bodies run, as usual, to create their test cases, but the bodies of the test cases do not, so no check is evaluated. The selected test cases (see filter_patterns) are listed under the names of their suites, as Catch2 lists them:

The header is Matching test cases: when there are filter patterns, and the suites without selected test cases are not listed. The nested test cases are not listed, since they are created by the bodies of their parents, which do not run. The list is made of plain lines, the same with both reporters and with all the verbosity levels, and is written to the console and to the output file, if any; no report is written, and run_suites() returns 0, 1 if a call was rejected or an exception escaped a suite body, which makes the list incomplete (the error is written in the list, as an error: line, or a # error: comment with the TAP reporter), or 2 after an option error, or if the filters selected no test case.

briefdescription.para: Path of the optional output file.

detaileddescription.para: Set by --output-file=<path> or --output-file <path>. When it is empty (the default), no file is written. The reporter opens the file when it is created by initialise(); if the file cannot be opened, the error is reported on stderr and on the console, no test is run, and runner::run_suites() returns 2.

briefdescription.para: The reporter that displays the results.

detaileddescription.para: Set by --reporter=<name> or --reporter <name>, where the name is tap or human.

briefdescription.para: The level of detail of the console output.

detaileddescription.para: Set by --silent, --quiet, or --verbose; when several are given, the last one takes effect.

briefdescription.para: The index in arguments_ of the first argument left to the application.

detaileddescription.para: Set by the parsing constructor, where the parsing of the µTest++ options ends; used by application_arguments().

briefdescription.para: The complete command line, including argv[0], if any.

detaileddescription.para: Filled by the parsing constructor with a copy of the argv[] strings; returned by arguments(), and used by application_arguments().

briefdescription.para: The errors found while parsing the command line.

detaileddescription.para: Appended by add_error(); returned by errors(), and tested by has_errors().

briefdescription.para: Whether an unknown option was found.

detaileddescription.para: Set by the parsing constructor, with the error; tested by has_unknown_option().

briefdescription.para: Copy constructor.

detaileddescription.para: Copies all the members, including the strings and the results of the parsing, so the copy initialises a runner exactly as the original does; the copy is independent of the original.

briefdescription.para: Constructs the options by parsing the command line.

detaileddescription.para: Starts from the defaults, and parses the µTest++ options (--reporter, --silent, --quiet, --verbose, --output-file, --colour, --color, --use-colour, --use-color, --filter, --list-tests, --list, --help, and -h). The parsing ends at the first argument that does not start with a dash (an application argument), or at the first -- alone; that argument, and all the following ones, are left to the application, and are available from application_arguments(). An option argument given separately (--reporter human) belongs to its option and does not end the parsing. Before that point, the arguments starting with a dash that are not µTest++ options are reported as unknown options; an application that receives such arguments first must precede them with --.

A missing option argument, an unknown reporter name, an unknown colour mode, a colour mode given separately after --colour or --color, or an unknown option, is recorded in errors(), and makes has_errors() true; the constructor writes nothing. The parsing continues, to record all the errors, but runner::initialise() then runs no test: it writes the errors on stderr, on the console, and in the output file, if any, followed, for an unknown option, by a line suggesting --help, and run_suites() returns 2.
The argv[] strings are copied, so they need not outlive the options.

argc
The argument count from main().
argv
The argument vector from main().
6.0.0
Scans the arguments after argv[0], in order, for:

listitem.para: --reporter=<name> or --reporter <name>, with tap (the default) or human;

--colour[=<when>], or its American spelling --color[=<when>], as in the GNU tools, with always, never, or auto (the default), and their GNU synonyms (yes and force, no and none, tty and if-tty); --colour alone means always;
--use-colour=<mode> or --use-colour <mode>, or the American spelling --use-color, the Catch2 and Boost UT alternative to --colour, with yes, no, or auto, or any of the --colour values;
--list-tests, or its short form --list, as in Catch2 and Boost UT, to list the test cases instead of running them;
--help, or its short form -h, to display the usage instead of running the tests.

detaileddescription.para: When an option is repeated, the last one takes effect, except --filter, whose patterns are all kept, in order, one per nesting level; --colour, --color, --use-colour, and --use-color set the same option. An option argument given separately is the next argument, whatever its content; --colour and --color accept their value only after =.

The parsing ends at the first argument that does not start with a dash, or at the first -- alone; the arguments from there on are left to the application, and are not interpreted, so they can be options of the application. The -- itself is not an application argument. An argument that starts with a dash, before that point, and is not a µTest++ option, is reported as an unknown option. The whole command line is copied into arguments_, to be listed by the reporter; the option values are copied from there.

A missing option argument, an unknown reporter name, an unknown colour mode, a colour mode given separately after --colour or --color, or an unknown option (any other argument that starts with a dash, including a single one), is recorded by add_error(), and the option is ignored; the parsing continues with the next argument, to record all the errors. Nothing is written by the constructor; the runner then writes the errors and refuses to run the tests.

briefdescription.para: Move constructor.

detaileddescription.para: Moves the strings and the vectors, and copies the other members; other is left valid, with unspecified strings.

briefdescription.para: Constructs the default options.

detaileddescription.para: The TAP reporter, the normal verbosity, no output file, automatic colours, no filter, and no command line; the test cases are run, not listed.

briefdescription.para: Destructor.

detaileddescription.para: Releases the owned strings.

briefdescription.para: Returns the arguments left to the application.

detaileddescription.para: The arguments that follow the µTest++ options on the command line: the first argument that does not start with a dash, if the parsing ended there, and all the following ones, unchanged, or, if the parsing ended at a -- alone, the arguments after it, which may start with --. The -- itself and argv[0] are not included. The span refers to the command line, so it is valid as long as the options are not modified or destroyed.

Parameters
None.
A span of the arguments; empty if there are none, or if the options were not parsed from a command line.
6.0.0
Returns the part of arguments_ that starts at application_begin_, or an empty span if there are none, including when the options were not parsed from a command line.

briefdescription.para: Returns the complete command line, including argv[0], if any.

detaileddescription.para: A copy of the argv[] strings of main(), set when the options are parsed from the command line; empty for the default options. When not empty, the reporters list it at the beginning of the report, and runner::add_top_suite() derives the default name of the top suite from its first element. The arguments left to the application are returned by application_arguments().
The command line is read-only, since application_arguments() depends on the position where the parsing ended, which would be stale if the strings were changed afterwards.

Parameters
None.
A reference to the strings; empty if the options were not parsed from a command line.
6.0.0
Returns the member arguments_, which is filled only by the parsing constructor.

briefdescription.para: Returns the errors found while parsing the command line.

detaileddescription.para: Each message is the text of the error, without the error: prefix and the newline, in the order of the arguments. The runner writes them on stderr and on the console when it refuses to run the tests.

Parameters
None.
A reference to the messages; empty if there were no errors.
6.0.0
Returns the errors_ member.

briefdescription.para: Checks whether errors were found while parsing the command line.

detaileddescription.para: The constructor only records the errors; when set, the runner runs no test and runner::run_suites() returns 2. Never set for the default options.

Parameters
None.
true if at least one error was found.
6.0.0
Returns whether the errors_ member is not empty.

briefdescription.para: Checks whether an unknown option was found while parsing the command line.

detaileddescription.para: Set together with the corresponding error; the runner then adds a line suggesting --help to the errors it writes on the console.

Parameters
None.
true if at least one unknown option was found.
6.0.0
Returns the unknown_option_ member.

briefdescription.para: Copy assignment operator.

detaileddescription.para: Replaces all the members with copies of those of other.

Not defaulted: it copies other with the copy constructor, and moves the copy into this instance, since the copy assignment of the vectors of strings uses std::copy, which triggers -Waggregate-return in the standard library headers of GCC on some targets. If the copy fails, this instance is not changed.

other
The instance to copy.
Reference to this instance.
6.0.0
Copies other with the copy constructor, and moves the copy into this instance; self-assignment is safe.

briefdescription.para: Move assignment operator.

detaileddescription.para: Moves the strings and the vectors, and copies the other members.

briefdescription.para: Records a command-line error.

detaileddescription.para: Appends the text to errors_; nothing is written, so that parsing the command line has no output.

before
The start of the message, without the error: prefix.
value
The variable part, usually an option or a value.
after
The end of the message, without the newline.
Returns
Nothing.
The message is only kept in errors_, so that the constructor has no output; the runner writes it on stderr and on the console, since the reporter does not exist yet.

briefdescription.para: The configuration of a test session, and its command-line parser.

detaileddescription.para: The options are usually constructed from the command line, by runner::initialise (argc, argv), which creates the selected reporter and starts the session:
The applications that do not have a command line, such as the embedded ones without semihosting arguments, can define the options directly, starting from the defaults:
The applications can also parse the command line themselves, and adjust the result before passing it to the runner:

The configuration members are public, since any combination of their values is valid; the command line and the results of the parsing (whether errors were found, whether an unknown option was found, and where the application arguments start) are private, since they depend on one another, and are read with the accessors.

The options own their strings (the command line, the path of the output file, and the filter patterns), so they do not depend on the lifetime of the caller's strings; the runner keeps its own copy of them.
